---
title: "Git and the paper trail"
---

Quartorium uses plain Git and nothing else, so it works with any Git host: Codeberg or a
self-hosted Forgejo, a university GitLab, GitHub, or a bare repository on a server. It never
uses a forge's API (pull requests, issues). Every step is an ordinary commit you can inspect
with any Git tool.

## Branches

| Branch | Contains | Who writes it |
|---|---|---|
| your main branch | **the paper**: always the latest agreed version | you (from RStudio, VS Code, …) and Quartorium, which keeps it up to date with the round |
| `quartorium/<paper>-<date>-<id>` | the **round**: the paper as it evolves during review | Quartorium, on behalf of each person |
| `quartorium/<round>--<name>-<id>` | one **reviewer's** copy, with everything they wrote, accepted or not | Quartorium, on behalf of that reviewer |

```{mermaid}
gitGraph
    commit id: "Paper draft"
    branch "quartorium/paper-round"
    checkout "quartorium/paper-round"
    branch "…--anna"
    checkout "…--anna"
    commit id: "Anna's edits (in progress)"
    commit id: "Anna finished her review"
    checkout "quartorium/paper-round"
    branch "…--bob"
    checkout "…--bob"
    commit id: "Bob's edits (in progress)"
    checkout "quartorium/paper-round"
    commit id: "Comment by Bob"
    commit id: "Anna's change accepted"
    commit id: "Bob's change declined"
    commit id: "Round finished"
    checkout main
    commit id: "Lena pushes from RStudio"
    checkout "quartorium/paper-round"
    merge main id: "Bring in the latest main"
    checkout main
    merge "quartorium/paper-round" id: "main kept up to date"
```

## What is committed, and when

Commits follow moments people understand, not timers. Typing never creates a commit: drafts
are saved on the server continuously and shown to others within seconds.

| Moment | Branch | Commit | Git author |
|---|---|---|---|
| A reviewer leaves the page, or doesn't type for 10 minutes | reviewer's | `Anna's edits (in progress)` | the reviewer |
| A reviewer clicks **Finish my review** | reviewer's | `Anna finished their review (3 suggested changes, 2 comments)` + their note | the reviewer |
| The lead leaves the page, or doesn't type for 10 minutes, after editing directly | round | `Lena's edits` | the lead |
| The lead **accepts** a suggestion | round | `Anna's change accepted: “…”` | **the person who wrote the text** |
| The lead **declines** a suggestion | round | `Bob's change declined: “…”` (no change to the file) | the lead |
| A reviewer withdraws their own suggestion | round | `Bob withdrew a change: “…”` | the reviewer |
| Comment, reply, resolve, reference request | round | `Comment by Anna on “…”: …`, `Reply by Bob: …`, `Anna resolved a comment` | the person |
| 👍 on a comment | round | bundled into the next commit | – |
| Someone pushes to main (checked every minute, and when the lead opens the paper) | round | `Bring in the latest main` (a merge commit) | Quartorium, or the lead with **Sync with main now** |
| The round has new commits, and main is kept up to date | main | none: main moves to the round's latest commit (a fast-forward) | – |
| **Finish round** | round | `Review round finished: …` with a summary | the lead |
| **Merge into main** (only when main is *not* kept up to date) | main | the same as above, on request | the lead |

The committer of every commit is "Quartorium". New commits are pushed to the remote within
about 30 seconds.

When a reviewer's copy is brought up to date with the round, the next commit on their branch
is a merge commit with the round as second parent, so `git log --graph` shows exactly which
version of the round they were working on.

### Why the person is the author

Accepted text is committed with the co-author as Git author. `git blame paper.qmd` therefore
shows, line by line, who wrote what, including sentences written by co-authors who have
never used Git. Decisions (declining, finishing a round) are authored by the lead who made
them.

### Comments are in the file

Open comment threads are stored in the `.qmd` itself, in an HTML comment at the end (see
[How .qmd files are changed](qmd-files.qmd#comments)). They travel with the paper through
branches and merges, and Quarto never renders them. When a round is finished, resolved
threads are removed from the file, and the commits that added them keep them in the history.

## Main stays up to date {#main}

Main is the paper. During a round, Quartorium keeps main and the round in step, both ways:

- **Your pushes come in.** When you push to main from RStudio or VS Code, Quartorium merges
  it into the round within a minute, or immediately when you open the paper in Quartorium.
  Changed code, new figures, new data and edited text all come along, and co-authors see
  them the next time they open their link.
- **The round goes out.** Accepted suggestions, your edits in the browser and comments are
  put on main as they are committed, normally as a fast-forward with no extra merge
  commits. A `git pull` in RStudio brings all of it, and the comments stay invisible in the
  rendered paper.

So nobody has to remember to merge, and your own copy never drifts far from what your
co-authors are reviewing.

### Working in RStudio during a round

Work the way you normally do with Git:

1. **Pull** at the start of a work session (RStudio: *Git → Pull*).
2. Change code, add figures, edit text. **Commit.**
3. **Pull again, then push.** If Quartorium put something on main in the meantime, Git asks
   you to pull before you can push, as with any co-author. Git merges it with your commits.
   That only stops for a decision if you edited the very lines that changed in the round.

Quartorium merges the paper **paragraph by paragraph**, not line by line, and merges comment
threads separately. Edits to different paragraphs never conflict, even neighbouring ones,
and neither do code, figures or other files. Quartorium only ever changes the one `.qmd`
under review.

If you and the round changed **the same paragraph** between two syncs, for example because
you rewrote a paragraph in RStudio while a co-author's version of it was being accepted,
**your version from main is kept**. The round's version is attached to that paragraph as a
comment from Quartorium, so you can compare them and copy from it. Reviewers who were
editing that paragraph keep their version as an *outdated* suggestion. Nothing is lost, and
the merge commit records both sides.

### When main is protected, or you'd rather merge yourself

Turn off **Round ▾ → Keep main up to date** for the repository. Your pushes still come into
the round, but main only changes when you choose **Round ▾ → Merge into main**, or when you
merge the branch `quartorium/…` with a pull/merge request on your Git host.

If your Git host refuses Quartorium's push to main (a protected branch), Quartorium turns
the setting off by itself and tells you which branch to merge.

## Rounds and links

*Start next round* creates a new round branch, from main if the last round is on main (as it
is when main is kept up to date), otherwise from the last round's branch. Each person's link moves to the new round, so
co-authors never need a new link. The finished round keeps a private read-only link for the
lead (**Round ▾ → Earlier rounds**).

## Looking at it with Git

```bash
git fetch origin
git log --graph --oneline origin/main 'origin/quartorium/*'   # the whole picture
git log --format='%an: %s' origin/quartorium/paper-2026-11-21-ab12   # one round, by person
git blame paper.qmd                                           # who wrote which line
git diff main origin/quartorium/paper-2026-11-21-ab12 -- paper.qmd   # what the round changed
```
